bodyHTML:
Greetings,

I just got mini.icons through the last update of lazyvim and would like to add icons to specific filetypes.
As a first test I wanted to add the ansible icons to filetype yaml.ansible.

What I did was adding the following to the lazyvim configuration:

return {
  {
    "echasnovski/mini.icons",
    opts = {
      filetype= {
        ['yaml.ansible'] = { glyph = '󱂚', hl = 'MiniIconsGrey' },
      },
    },
  },
}

Icon would be nf-md-ansible.

But for some reason that does not work for me. Doing the same for filetype yaml instead of yaml.ansible works, but then all my yaml files have the ansible icon which is not what I want to achieve.
It seems to me that for some reason mini.icons only sees the yaml filetype and not my yaml.ansible.

To detect the ansible filetype I am setting those through vim.add.filetype in a custom config in lazyvim. Which is correctly identified by the ansiblels.

Does anyone has a hint for me what I might be doing wrong?
Thanks in advance.

comment_data.body:
Hi!

First, just to make sure, is "yaml.ansible" is indeed a filetype? What it means is that when you open a target file, it has `'filetype'` options equal to `'yaml.ansimble'`. Does it say so after you execute `:=vim.bo.filetype`?

Second (if the first one is true), where do you expect it to be shown? If in the file explorer, then chances are that it uses "file" category. In this case, it has [certain order of preference](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/d187614ecee84ef8d7456339ed7ce1160d054310/doc/mini-icons.txt#L292-L296) and if the file name ends with plain "yaml" or "yml" extension, then it stops on the second step as those are manually [tracked extensions](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/d187614ecee84ef8d7456339ed7ce1160d054310/lua/mini/icons.lua#L658-L659) (you can see those with `:=MiniIcons.list('extension')`).

The reason it was added to manually tracked list is because it is fairly common (like, for example, around 3% of all files in [this benchmark project](https://github.com/Yggdroot/a_large_project)) and always relying on `vim.filetype.match()` might get slow-ish.

comment_data.body:
So, I've removed 'yml' and 'yaml' from the list of built-in (manually tracked) extensions, but upon investigation I don't think this will help your use case. Based on [this filetype detection](https://github.com/mfussenegger/nvim-ansible/blob/main/ftdetect/ansible.lua) for 'yaml.ansible' it requires checking full path, which is currently not supported: only basename is taken into account for "file" and "directory" category.

The reason for this is to make better use of caching: with full paths cache will not be reused for files with same basenames (which I think is a more common occurrence).

I'll make some profiling (both memory and speed) for when full path is used and get back to you. Hope to do this in the near future.

comment_data.bodyHTML:
@mstinsky, thanks to a series of refactors and optimizations (see this comment if you are curious which ones), this is now possible on latest main with a few necessary setup tweaks. Here is a setup that makes it work:

local ext_skip = { yml = true }
require('mini.icons').setup({
  use_file_extension = function(ext, _) return not ext_skip[ext:lower()] end,
})

This setup basically tells 'mini.icons' that 'yml' filetype should be ignored during "file" resolution which results in always relying on vim.filetype.match() output (which is essentially what is needed here). See help entry for more details.

Assuming the vim.filetype.add({ pattern = { ['.*/roles/.*/tasks/.*%.ya?ml'] = 'yaml.ansible' } }) filetype detection set up, here is how it looks in latest 'mini.files':

Note that this requires that MiniIcons.get('file', ...) is called with a string that satisfies the pattern matching rules, which is usually a full path. So this might not work if 'mini.icons' user (usually plugin) calls it only with basename.

This question/issue was the main driving force for making those (overall positive) changes happen, so thanks for creating it!

reply_data.body:
> So it seems neo-tree.nvim is calling mini.icons with different path? Not sure how all the components are interacting with each other.
> Ill need to dig around a bit to see if I can get it to work somehow.

'nvim-neo-tree/neo-tree.nvim' doe not yet have direct support for 'mini.icons'. See nvim-neo-tree/neo-tree.nvim#1510 and nvim-neo-tree/neo-tree.nvim#1527. So what you currently see is the effect of mocked 'nvim-web-devicons' module via [`MiniIcons.mock_nvim_web_devicons()`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/e24ec1fcf885990fec1a993fe8304a033fd1806d/doc/mini-icons.txt#L440).

What I'd assume to happen is indeed that in both cases `MiniIcons.get('file', 'deploy.yml')` is called and in both cases is treated as relative path to the root. Hence the first case does not match (as its full paths is assumed to be '~/ws/marc/ansible/control/deploy.yml') and the second case it does match.

All in all, for take proper advantage of this feature, `get()` *must* be called with full path. Like it is done in 'mini.files' :wink:

comment_data.bodyHTML:
@mstinsky, there was a slight change in how use_file_extension operates. It is now explicitly called once, even if extension is compound or file has dots. Plus extension is now converted to lowercase (as this is what is needed in 99% of cases while the second argument with the file name is supplied as is).

The approach with ext_skip and return not ext_skip[ext:lower()] will still work in most cases when there is only single dot in a basename (like 'roles/a/tasks/hello.yml'. However, it fails on rare cases like 'roles/a/tasks/hello.extradot.yml'.

The suggested way now is to perform explicit string manipulation before comparing. So in your case it would be something like use_file_extension = function(ext) return ext:sub(-3) ~= 'yml' and ext:sub(-4) ~= 'yaml' end.
